q: Why do solar module model numbers in India now end in a four-letter country code?
title: Solar module model numbers with country codes
short: Under an MNRE procedure of 1 October 2026, solar module model numbers registered with BIS carry a four-character suffix: two letters for the country where the module was made and two for the country that made its cells. One suffixed model cannot mix cells from different countries.
audience: Buyers and EPC contractors checking module paperwork

ul: Format: original model number, a hyphen, then MMCC.
MM is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country of module manufacture.
CC is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country where the cells in that bill of materials were made.
Example: a module made in India with Indian cells ends in -ININ.
A model whose bills of materials use cells from different countries must be split into separate suffixed models.
Cells from more than one maker are allowed under one model only if all those makers are in the same country and the approved bill of materials names each one.
Existing BIS registered models must add the suffixed model numbers. If the change only removes or separates already approved cells, no fresh testing is needed; the lab issues a supplementary report.

p: The suffix lets you see from the label and datasheet where the cells came from, which matters for ALMM List-II and domestic content checks. If a datasheet shows no suffix on a model sold after the procedure, ask the seller why.

example.title: Reading two model numbers (illustrative)
lines: XYZ-550-ININ: module made in India, cells made in India
XYZ-550-INCN: module made in India, cells made in China
The two are separate BIS registered models, each with its own bill of materials
example.note: XYZ-550 is a made-up model used only to show the suffix.

senseible: Senseible can hold your module datasheets and invoices with the solar installation record, so the model number and its suffix are on file if a lender or buyer asks.
